result.title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) often present synthesized answers without making their supporting evidence easy to inspect. We study how features of these answers relate to users' subsequent accepting, checking, and challenging in 489,283 assistant-user response pairs from ShareChat and WildChat. Broad attribution language appears in 31.9% of qualifying responses, compared with explicit URLs in 1.33%, revealing a gap between claims of grounding and preserved inspectable support. Attribution, uncertainty, and other response cues generally accompany both checking and challenging; only uncertainty shows a small statistically distinguishable pooled association favoring checking. Within Technical Help, uncertainty favors checking relative to challenging; refusals and reasoning traces favor challenging in Seeking Information. Scrutiny is concentrated in some conversations, while its apparent turn-to-turn persistence becomes much smaller when conversation-level differences and response ordering are examined separately. These results suggest that supporting verification requires attention to what evidence can be inspected, which question a user is trying to resolve, and the history of the interaction.

AI.brief_summary: 该文分析 ShareChat 与 WildChat 上约 49 万条助手—用户对话对，考察助手的归因语言、显式 URL、不确定性等线索与用户随后接受、核查、质疑行为的关系，并比较对话层与轮次层的持续性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「声称有据」与「可检视证据」之间的落差，以及对核查/质疑触发条件的区分，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与证据呈现方式的评价目标提供参照，但对象是用户行为而非模型内部推理状态，需较多核查。
